intro: Public research is mixed. Use it as caution and context — not as a marketing multiplier.

items.title: METR — Early-2025 AI on experienced open-source developers
items.claim: RCT on real issues in familiar large repos: allowing AI (often Cursor + frontier models) made experienced developers about 19% slower — while they still believed they were faster.
items.use: Humbling baseline for wall-clock on familiar tickets.

items.title: Peng et al. — GitHub Copilot controlled experiment
items.claim: On constrained coding tasks, Copilot users finished substantially faster in a lab setting — a different problem class than multi-hour work in mature codebases.
items.use: Shows assistance can win on narrow tasks.

items.title: Enterprise Copilot field experiments (throughput)
items.claim: Field studies report higher pull-request throughput for assisted developers — volume is not the same as embedded proof quality.

items.title: Cursor adoption DiD (preprint discussion)
items.claim: Observational work on agentic IDE adoption reports early activity spikes with warnings about complexity/debt if review quality slips.
items.use: Do not confuse LOC spikes with sustainable capability.

readingOrder: Start with METR if you are about to claim a universal speedup.
Read a Copilot lab/field paper to see where assistance clearly helps.
Return to your capability map and proof pass rate — local truth beats borrowed multipliers.
